questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy has passed large, painless, dark red stools three times in 2 days. He is pale but playful, and his abdomen is soft and not tender. Laboratory results: hemoglobin 8.6 g/dL, platelets 320,000/mm³, prothrombin time 12 seconds (normal). A technetium-99m pertechnetate scan shows a small area of uptake in the right lower quadrant, separate from the stomach. At surgery, a pouch with all layers of the bowel wall arises from the antimesenteric border of the distal ileum. Failure of which embryonic structure to involute most likely explains this lesion?
questions.explanation: A **true diverticulum** on the antimesenteric side of the distal ileum is a **Meckel diverticulum**, a remnant of the **vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct**, which normally links the midgut to the yolk sac and closes early in fetal life. The pertechnetate scan finds **ectopic gastric mucosa**, whose acid ulcerates nearby ileum and causes painless bleeding. The **allantois** is the tempting distractor because it also ends at the umbilicus, but its remnant (the **urachus**) connects to the bladder and causes urine leakage or cysts, not ileal bleeding.
questions.explanation_pt: Um **divertículo verdadeiro** na borda antimesentérica do íleo distal é um **divertículo de Meckel**, resquício do **ducto vitelino (onfalomesentérico)**, que normalmente liga o intestino médio ao saco vitelino e se fecha cedo na vida fetal. A cintilografia com pertecnetato detecta **mucosa gástrica ectópica**, cujo ácido ulcera o íleo vizinho e causa sangramento indolor. O **alantoide** é o distrator tentador porque também termina no umbigo, mas seu resquício (o **úraco**) se liga à bexiga e causa saída de urina ou cistos, não sangramento ileal.

questions.stem: A 2-day-old boy with Down syndrome has not passed meconium. His abdomen is distended and he feeds poorly. On digital rectal exam, the anal canal feels tight and the rectum is empty; when the finger is removed, gas and stool come out explosively. A contrast enema shows a narrow rectum and sigmoid colon with a dilated colon above them. A rectal suction biopsy is done. Which finding is most likely?
choices: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosal plexus
Normal ganglion cells with thick, sticky meconium in the lumen
Noncaseating granulomas through the full bowel wall
Mucosal necrosis with gas bubbles in the bowel wall
Crypt abscesses with neutrophils limited to the mucosa
questions.explanation: This is **Hirschsprung disease**: **neural crest cells** did not reach the distal colon, so the rectum and a continuous segment above it have **no ganglion cells** and cannot relax. A suction biopsy samples mucosa and submucosa, so it shows **absent submucosal (Meissner) ganglion cells**, often with thick nerve fibers. **Meconium ileus** is the tempting distractor because it also delays meconium, but it is linked to **cystic fibrosis**, blocks the terminal ileum with sticky meconium, and the ganglion cells are normal.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **doença de Hirschsprung**: as **células da crista neural** não chegaram ao cólon distal, então o reto e um segmento contínuo acima dele **não têm células ganglionares** e não relaxam. A biópsia por sucção amostra mucosa e submucosa, então mostra **ausência de células ganglionares do plexo submucoso (de Meissner)**, muitas vezes com fibras nervosas espessadas. O **íleo meconial** é o distrator tentador porque também atrasa a eliminação de mecônio, mas está associado à **fibrose cística**, obstrui o íleo terminal com mecônio espesso e as células ganglionares são normais.

questions.stem: A 3-week-old girl who had been feeding well suddenly starts vomiting bright green fluid. Over a few hours she becomes irritable and then lethargic. An upper GI contrast study shows the duodenojejunal junction to the right of the midline, and the contrast narrows in a spiral, corkscrew pattern in the proximal small bowel. Without prompt surgery, ischemic necrosis would most likely involve the bowel supplied by which artery?
questions.explanation: The duodenojejunal junction lying right of the midline shows **malrotation**, and the corkscrew pattern shows **midgut volvulus**. The midgut hangs on a narrow mesentery, so it twists around its own artery, the **superior mesenteric artery**; the distal duodenum, jejunum, ileum, cecum, ascending colon and proximal transverse colon can all become ischemic. The **celiac trunk** is tempting because the obstruction is near the duodenum, but it supplies the foregut (stomach, proximal duodenum, liver), which is above the twist and keeps its blood flow.
questions.explanation_pt: A junção duodenojejunal à direita da linha média indica **má rotação**, e o padrão em saca-rolhas indica **volvo de intestino médio**. O intestino médio fica preso a um mesentério estreito, então gira em torno da sua própria artéria, a **artéria mesentérica superior**; duodeno distal, jejuno, íleo, ceco, cólon ascendente e cólon transverso proximal podem ficar isquêmicos. O **tronco celíaco** é tentador porque a obstrução está perto do duodeno, mas ele irriga o intestino anterior (estômago, duodeno proximal, fígado), que fica acima da torção e mantém o fluxo sanguíneo.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman has had three episodes of acute pancreatitis in 2 years. She does not drink alcohol and takes no medicines. Tests between episodes: triglycerides 140 mg/dL (normal), calcium 9.4 mg/dL (normal), ALT 22 U/L (normal) and alkaline phosphatase 80 U/L (normal). Ultrasound shows no gallstones. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography shows that the large duct draining the body and tail of the pancreas empties through the minor papilla. A short, separate duct from part of the pancreatic head empties through the major papilla. Which developmental error best explains these findings?
choices: Ventral pancreatic bud forming a ring around the second part of the duodenum
Failure of the duodenal lumen to recanalize
Ectopic pancreatic tissue in a vitelline duct remnant
Junction of the bile and pancreatic ducts outside the duodenal wall
Failure of the ventral and dorsal pancreatic ducts to fuse
questions.explanation: This is **pancreas divisum**: the ducts of the **ventral and dorsal pancreatic buds do not fuse**, so most of the gland drains through the dorsal duct and the small **minor papilla**. Most people with divisum have no symptoms, but in some the minor papilla is too narrow for this flow, and the backup can cause recurrent pancreatitis once common causes (alcohol, gallstones, high triglycerides, high calcium) are ruled out. **Annular pancreas** is the tempting distractor, but a ring of ventral bud tissue narrows the duodenum itself and does not create two separate duct systems.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **pâncreas divisum**: os ductos dos **brotos pancreáticos ventral e dorsal não se fundem**, então a maior parte da glândula drena pelo ducto dorsal e pela pequena **papila menor**. A maioria das pessoas com divisum é assintomática, mas em algumas a papila menor é estreita demais para esse fluxo, e a estase pode causar pancreatite recorrente depois de afastadas as causas comuns (álcool, cálculos biliares, hipertrigliceridemia, hipercalcemia). O **pâncreas anular** é o distrator tentador, mas o anel de tecido do broto ventral estreita o próprio duodeno e não cria dois sistemas ductais separados.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man with cirrhosis from long-term alcohol use has a swollen abdomen. Examination shows shifting dullness, a large spleen, and dilated, tortuous veins that spread out from the umbilicus across the abdominal wall. Which portal-side vessels carry blood into these abdominal wall veins?
questions.explanation: Veins radiating from the umbilicus are **caput medusae**. In portal hypertension, blood flows from the left branch of the portal vein through the **paraumbilical veins**, which run in the falciform ligament along the ligamentum teres, into the **epigastric veins** of the abdominal wall. The **left gastric vein** is the tempting distractor because it is the most dangerous collateral, but it connects with esophageal veins and causes **esophageal varices**, not veins around the umbilicus.
questions.explanation_pt: Veias que se irradiam a partir do umbigo são a **cabeça de medusa** (*caput medusae*). Na hipertensão portal, o sangue flui do ramo esquerdo da veia porta pelas **veias paraumbilicais**, que correm no ligamento falciforme junto ao ligamento redondo, para as **veias epigástricas** da parede abdominal. A **veia gástrica esquerda** é o distrator tentador por ser a colateral mais perigosa, mas ela se comunica com as veias esofágicas e causa **varizes esofágicas**, não veias periumbilicais.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man is brought in after a motorcycle crash. His blood pressure is 82/50 mm Hg and his pulse is 128/min. At laparotomy, there is a deep tear in the back of the right lobe of the liver. The surgeon clamps the free edge of the lesser omentum. Dark blood keeps welling up from behind the liver at about the same rate. Which vessel is the most likely source of the ongoing bleeding?
questions.explanation: Clamping the free edge of the lesser omentum (the **hepatoduodenal ligament**) is the **Pringle maneuver**; it stops inflow from the **proper hepatic artery** and **portal vein**. Bleeding that continues after the clamp points to vessels outside the ligament: the **hepatic veins** or the retrohepatic **inferior vena cava**, which drain blood out of the back of the liver. The **portal vein** is the tempting distractor because the blood is dark and venous, but the clamp already blocks it.
questions.explanation_pt: Clampear a borda livre do omento menor (o **ligamento hepatoduodenal**) é a **manobra de Pringle**; ela interrompe o influxo da **artéria hepática própria** e da **veia porta**. Sangramento que persiste após o clampeamento indica vasos fora do ligamento: as **veias hepáticas** ou a **veia cava inferior** retro-hepática, que drenam o sangue da face posterior do fígado. A **veia porta** é o distrator tentador porque o sangue é escuro e venoso, mas o clampe já a bloqueia.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man has an upper endoscopy for indigestion. Biopsies are taken from several sites, and one container arrives at the laboratory without a label. Under the microscope, the mucosa has finger-like villi and crypts. The submucosa is packed with branched glands made of pale, mucus-filled cells, and their ducts open into the crypts. Lymphoid follicles are few. From which part of the gut was this biopsy most likely taken?
questions.explanation: Mucus glands in the **submucosa** are **Brunner glands**, which are found in the **duodenum**. They release **bicarbonate-rich mucus** that helps neutralize the acid leaving the stomach. The **jejunum** is the tempting distractor because it also has villi and crypts, but it has no submucosal glands. The terminal ileum has large lymphoid aggregates (**Peyer patches**), the gastric antrum has no villi, and the colon has crypts without villi.
questions.explanation_pt: Glândulas mucosas na **submucosa** são as **glândulas de Brunner**, encontradas no **duodeno**. Elas secretam **muco rico em bicarbonato**, que ajuda a neutralizar o ácido que sai do estômago. O **jejuno** é o distrator tentador porque também tem vilosidades e criptas, mas não tem glândulas na submucosa. O íleo terminal tem grandes agregados linfoides (**placas de Peyer**), o antro gástrico não tem vilosidades e o cólon tem criptas sem vilosidades.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman has had fullness after meals and vomiting of bile-stained food for 3 weeks. Three months ago she had spinal fusion surgery for scoliosis. Measurements: height 165 cm; weight 44 kg now and 54 kg before surgery; body mass index 16.2 kg/m². Her symptoms improve when she lies on her left side. CT shows a dilated stomach and proximal duodenum, with an abrupt narrowing where the duodenum crosses the midline in front of the spine. Which part of the duodenum is compressed, and by which structures?
choices: Second part, by an enlarged head of the pancreas
Third part, between the SMA and the aorta
First part, by a thickened gastroduodenal artery
Fourth part, by a short suspensory ligament
Second part, by a ring of ventral pancreatic tissue
questions.explanation: This is **superior mesenteric artery syndrome**. The **third (horizontal) part of the duodenum** crosses the midline between the **aorta** behind and the **SMA** in front. Rapid weight loss shrinks the fat pad in this angle, and surgery that straightens the spine can narrow it, so the duodenum is squeezed. **Annular pancreas** is the tempting distractor because it also blocks the duodenum, but it is a birth defect that narrows the second part, which lies to the right of the spine, not at the midline.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se da **síndrome da artéria mesentérica superior**. A **terceira porção (horizontal) do duodeno** cruza a linha média entre a **aorta**, atrás, e a **AMS**, na frente. A perda rápida de peso reduz o coxim de gordura nesse ângulo, e a cirurgia que corrige a curvatura da coluna pode estreitá-lo, então o duodeno é comprimido. O **pâncreas anular** é o distrator tentador porque também obstrui o duodeno, mas é um defeito congênito que estreita a segunda porção, situada à direita da coluna, e não na linha média.
